text:
Fall 2026


  Syllabus 




University of South Florida

A theory-based introduction to mathematical statistics covering probability distributions, transformations of random variables, sampling distributions, and asymptotic results. The course develops statistical inference through point estimation, confidence intervals, properties of estimators, and hypothesis testing.

Mathematical Statistics Probability Statistical Inference





Spring 2026


  Syllabus 




University of South Florida

An introduction to the theory and practice of sample survey design, including simple random, systematic, stratified, cluster, and two-phase sampling. Additional topics include ratio and regression estimation, nonresponse, complex surveys, variance estimation, and implementation using statistical software.

Survey Sampling Sampling Design Estimation





Fall 2024


  Syllabus 




University of South Florida

A computational introduction to applied statistics with an emphasis on R programming and data analysis. Topics include data manipulation and visualization, simulation, probability distributions, statistical inference, ANOVA, linear regression, logistic regression, and interpretation of statistical output.

Applied Statistics Data Analysis Statistical Modeling

title: Xiankui Yang
text:
About Me
I am a Postdoctoral Scholar in the Department of Mathematics and Statistics at the University of South Florida. I received my Ph.D. in Mathematics with a concentration in Statistics from the University of South Florida. My research interests include statistical methodology, optimal experimental design, computational statistics, optimization, and machine learning. My current research focuses on developing computational methods for multi-objective optimal design and exploring optimization-based approaches for statistical modeling and learning.

title: Xiankui Yang
text:
My research focuses on statistical methodology, optimal experimental design, computational statistics, optimization, and machine learning. I am particularly interested in developing computational methods for complex statistical problems, including multi-objective design optimization and robust statistical modeling.








01


Optimal Experimental Design


My research in optimal experimental design focuses on constructing efficient designs for statistical modeling and scientific experimentation. It considers multiple design objectives, computational optimization, and the trade-offs that arise when different statistical criteria must be satisfied simultaneously. This work aims to make optimal design methods more flexible and computationally practical for complex experimental settings.


Optimal Design Multi-objective Optimization Pareto Front


▶ View related publication



Multi-Objective Optimal Experimental Design


This work develops particle-swarm-based optimization methods for constructing Pareto-optimal experimental designs under multiple competing criteria, including I-, G-, and D-optimality. The goal is to efficiently characterize trade-offs among different design objectives and provide a collection of candidate designs rather than a single optimal solution.


Input-Response Experimental Design


Yang, X., Lu, L., & Anderson-Cook, C. M. (2024). Input-response space-filling designs incorporating response uncertainty. Statistical Analysis and Data Mining: The ASA Data Science Journal, 17(1), e11648. DOI

Develops an input-response space-filling design framework that incorporates response uncertainty, allowing the design to account for coverage in both the experimental input space and the resulting response space.









02


Sequential Experimental Design


My research in sequential experimental design focuses on efficient data collection when experiments can be conducted and updated over multiple stages. It includes space-filling design, adaptive selection of new experimental points, and design augmentation based on information already collected. These methods are particularly useful for exploring complex design spaces while controlling experimental cost and improving the information obtained from each stage.


Sequential Design Space-Filling Design Adaptive Design Design Augmentation


▶ View related publications



Space-Filling Design Methodology


Yang, X., Lu, L., & Anderson-Cook, C. M. (2026). Quick Input-Response Space-Filling (QIRSF) Designs. Quality and Reliability Engineering International. DOI

Develops a fast and scalable input-response space-filling approach that jointly considers input-space coverage and anticipated response behavior while substantially reducing computational cost.



Yang, X., Lu, L., & Anderson-Cook, C. M. (2025). A scalable algorithm for generating non-uniform space-filling designs. Journal of Quality Technology, 1–19. DOI

Develops a scalable method for non-uniform space-filling designs that allows experimental points to be concentrated in regions requiring greater attention.



Yang, X., Lu, L., & Anderson-Cook, C. M. (2024). Input-response space-filling designs incorporating response uncertainty. Statistical Analysis and Data Mining: The ASA Data Science Journal, 17(1), e11648. DOI

Extends input-response space-filling design by incorporating uncertainty in anticipated responses into the design construction process.









03


Statistical Methodology & Applications


My research in statistical methodology connects statistical modeling with real-world data analysis. It includes regression and longitudinal methods, statistical inference, and data-driven approaches for understanding complex relationships in observational data. Applications have covered transportation, mobility, travel behavior, equity, resilience, and other social and behavioral problems, demonstrating how statistical methods can support both scientific understanding and practical decision-making.


Statistical Modeling Transportation Longitudinal Analysis Applied Statistics


▶ View related publications



Transportation & Mobility Applications


Yang, X., Chen, P., & Zhang, Y. (2023). How mentally healthy were we during the pandemic? Findings from changed travel behavior. Journal of Transport & Health, 29, 101587. DOI

Examines the relationship between changes in travel behavior and mental health during the COVID-19 pandemic, highlighting how changes in daily mobility were associated with individual well-being.



Chen, P., Yang, X., Zhang, Y., & Hud, S. (2025). The resiliency of transit and ride-hailing system through the coronavirus pandemic: Lessons from six large US cities. Case Studies on Transport Policy, 101470. DOI

Examines transit and ride-hailing systems across six large U.S. cities to study transportation-system responsiveness and resilience during the COVID-19 pandemic.



Tao, R., Yang, X., Hao, F., & Chen, P. (2024). Demographic disparity and influences in electric vehicle adoption: A Florida case study. Transportation Research Part D: Transport and Environment, 136, 104465. DOI

Uses vehicle registration, demographic, and socioeconomic information to investigate disparities in electric vehicle adoption across Florida.



Chen, P., Yang, X., & Zhang, Y. (2024). Exploring the interconnection between telecommuting, trip reduction, and transportation equity amidst the coronavirus pandemic. Transportation Letters, 1–11. DOI

Investigates relationships among telecommuting, changes in travel behavior, and transportation equity across different population groups.



Chen, P., & Yang, X. (2023). Revisit employer-based travel demand management: A longitudinal analysis. Transport Policy, 131, 22–31. DOI

Uses longitudinal data to evaluate employer-based travel demand management strategies and their influence on commuting behavior.









04


Computational Statistics & Machine Learning


My research in computational statistics and machine learning combines statistical methodology with modern computational tools for analyzing complex data. It includes robust statistical modeling, optimization, interpretable machine learning, survival analysis, and neural-network methods. A central interest is understanding not only predictive performance, but also model robustness and interpretation, with applications ranging from behavioral and transportation data to biomedical and health-related classification problems.


Machine Learning Robust Modeling Interpretable AI Scientific Computing


▶ View related research & publications



Robust Logistic Modeling and Neural Networks


This work compares conventional likelihood and cross-entropy approaches with alternative distance-based estimation methods. The methods are evaluated through simulation studies and real-world classification problems, including biomedical and health-related data, with attention to robustness, predictive performance, and computational implementation.


Machine Learning Applications


Chen, P., Yang, X., Hao, F., & Tao, R. (2026). Decoding electric vehicle adoption using XGBoost and SHAP analysis. Travel Behaviour and Society, 42, 101125. DOI

Combines XGBoost with SHAP analysis to identify and interpret demographic, socioeconomic, and behavioral factors associated with electric vehicle adoption.



Chen, P., & Yang, X. (2025). Premature casual carpooling in Texas: analyzing customer churn in the Metropia experiment with survival analysis and machine learning. Case Studies on Transport Policy, 101587. DOI

Combines survival analysis and machine learning to identify behavioral, usage, and contextual factors associated with premature customer churn.
